comp_disc_analysis.notes:
[chunk 1/3] Source is MSFT DEF 14A (2024-10-24), Compensation Discussion & Analysis section. Key SIFI-material findings:

1. PARTNERSHIP WEB: Microsoft explicitly names OpenAI, Cohere, Databricks, Mistral, Meta, NVIDIA, Oracle, SAP, and G42 as strategic partners. Azure OpenAI Service is used by 65%+ of Fortune 500 — significant customer concentration signal for OpenAI's dependency on Azure.

2. NVIDIA DEEP INTEGRATION: 'Deep partnership with Nvidia spans the entirety of the Copilot stack... including Nvidia's DGX cloud natively integrating with Microsoft Fabric' — supplier concentration / single-source dependency signal.

3. G42 MEGA-DEAL: Described as 'the largest commercial agreement in Microsoft's history' with an accompanying Intergovernmental Assurance Agreement. $30B in government investment announcements across 12 governments. Geopolitical risk (G42 is UAE-based). Separate $5B infrastructure deployment in SEA/Kenya with G42.

4. CIRCULARITY: Microsoft is simultaneously OpenAI's primary compute provider (Azure), a major investor in OpenAI, and a reseller of OpenAI models via Azure OpenAI Service — classic investor/customer/supplier triangle.

5. Exec comp section is otherwise routine — no related-party compensation arrangements flagged; Nadella voluntarily reduced his own bonus by 50%+ citing cybersecurity urgency (security as top strategic priority signal).
[chunk 2/3] This DEF 14A section is entirely a Compensation Discussion & Analysis covering PSA/SA equity award structures, executive pay tables, CEO pay ratio, pay-versus-performance disclosures, and severance plan terms for Microsoft's Named Executive Officers (Nadella, Hood, Althoff, Smith, Young). The only named external entity of potential SIFI relevance is Activision Blizzard, mentioned solely to note that ~11,825 acquired employees were excluded from the median-employee calculation for CEO pay ratio purposes — a routine disclosure footnote, not a material business relationship, investment, off-balance-sheet structure, or counterparty concentration risk. No SPVs, JVs, AI-lab investments, supplier/customer concentration, hidden leverage, revenue roundtripping, or capex commitments are disclosed or implied in this section. Nothing meets the SIFI-materiality threshold defined in the extraction rules.
[chunk 3/3] This DEF 14A section covers Microsoft's Pay Versus Performance disclosure, equity compensation plan information, and principal shareholder table. The content is entirely boilerplate compensation disclosure — executive pay calculations under SEC Pay vs. Performance rules, equity plan share counts, and routine 5%+ shareholder disclosures (Vanguard at 8.95%, BlackRock at 7.30%). None of this meets the SIFI-material threshold: no SPVs, no AI lab investments named, no customer/supplier concentration, no off-balance-sheet arrangements, no circular dependencies, no revenue roundtripping, and no capex commitments. The Vanguard and BlackRock ownership disclosures are standard passive index-fund ownership and do not represent strategic or related-party arrangements. No SIFI-material entities to extract.

beneficial_owners.notes:
[chunk 1/3] Extraction from MSFT DEF 14A (2024-10-24). This is the Beneficial Ownership and Proposals section. The beneficial ownership table itself contains no SIFI-material entities—it lists director and executive shareholdings, all below 1% except CEO Satya Nadella (867,989 shares). The significant SIFI-material content is in the Shareholder Proposals section (Proposals 4–7), which disclose: (1) $22B IVAS military contract with execution risks and employee resistance; (2) AI/ML facilitation of oil and gas expansion with staff turnover risk; (3) Saudi Arabia datacenter expansion into human rights hotspot. Audit fees to Deloitte increased from $45.6M (2023) to $56.3M (2024), indicating heightened audit scope. No off-balance-sheet entities, investments in AI labs, or counterparty circularity detected in this section. Related-party transactions are reviewed but not detailed in this excerpt."
[chunk 2/3] EXTRACTION SUMMARY: Microsoft DEF 14A (2024-10-24) captures three SIFI-material risk clusters: (1) CUSTOMER_CONCENTRATION in fossil fuels (ExxonMobil, Schlumberger, Chevron named; broader oil-and-gas exposure for decades disclosed). (2) AI MISINFORMATION & DATA LIABILITY: $13B OpenAI investment creates reputational and legal exposure—Bing Chat had ~10% error rate, Copilot produced 'bizarre, disturbing' responses, NY Times lawsuit alleges copyright infringement. (3) REPUTATIONAL RISK via greenwashing accusations (climate commitments vs. continued fossil fuel tech deployment). No off-balance-sheet entities, capex commitments, or circularity patterns detected in this narrative section. The shareholder proposals themselves (not management recommendations) articulated these risks. Employee concerns also noted (internal opposition to fossil fuel partnerships). Section 230 liability shield uncertainty flagged by legal experts; EU AI Act compliance reporting requirement introduced for 2025."
[chunk 3/3] No SIFI-material entities identified. The source text is a standard proxy cover page containing only boilerplate information: shareholder meeting logistics, proxy appointment instructions (Sandra E. Peterson and Satya Nadella as proxies), and procedural voting language. No business relationships, investments, customer/supplier dependencies, related-party arrangements, or material counterparty data are disclosed. This section does not meet the threshold for extraction.
